headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because aci can egress CRM/email data while ComfyUI is offline-only but can still consume unverified inputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can route content through MCP/direct function calls and handles email/CRM data; ComfyUI has no shared channel or parser bridge by default. The main injection path is indirect: if aci forwards untrusted text into ComfyUI workflows or prompts, ComfyUI may treat it as input. This is plausible but not documented as a default bridge, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF aci forwards untrusted email/CRM text into a ComfyUI workflow or prompt field
IF an operator manually copies aci output into ComfyUI inputs
mitigations: Add a strict allowlist for fields passed from aci to ComfyUI
Strip instructions and markup from aci outputs before reuse
Use a human review step for any text-to-image prompt transfer
requires-engineering: add provenance tags between systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data and has broad network egress; ComfyUI is offline by default but still reads local model files. If both are run in a shared workspace or same account, sensitive aci data can be exposed to ComfyUI inputs or artifacts, and aci can transmit data outward. The pair therefore creates a realistic exfiltration path with sensitive business data.
conditions: IF aci and ComfyUI share a workspace, mount, or operator account
IF aci forwards CRM/email/support text into ComfyUI prompts or files
mitigations: Separate workspaces and OS users for the two agents
Disable aci access to sensitive sources during image generation tasks
Review any prompt or file handoff before execution
Log and alert on outbound requests from aci
requires-engineering: add per-agent data-loss prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and broad API-based actions, while ComfyUI does not write filesystems, modify git, or spawn subprocesses. Their mutable surfaces do not overlap materially in the profiles, so direct write/write conflict is unlikely. Any conflict would require an external shared resource not shown here, so low is the right bound.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator maps both agents onto the same mutable API resource
IF aci is configured to write into a shared directory outside the shown profile
mitigations: Assign separate API credentials per agent
Avoid shared mutable folders or git repos
Serialize any shared-resource updates with a lock
Check for duplicate writes in the orchestrator

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar content that ComfyUI could ingest as prompts or workflow text, but ComfyUI is not documented as acting on those outputs autonomously. The cascade is therefore plausible when operators reuse aci output without verification, yet not inherently action-taking. Medium fits because the output can propagate errors into downstream work products.
conditions: IF aci output is copied into ComfyUI prompts or workflow parameters without review
IF generated text from aci is treated as authoritative input by the operator
mitigations: Require a verification step before reusing aci-generated text
Use templates with fixed prompt slots instead of free-form text
Keep a manual approval checkpoint before ComfyUI runs
requires-engineering: add schema validation for transferred fields

E_compliance.rationale: aci explicitly handles CRM, email, support, and calendar data and has broad egress, while ComfyUI is offline and model-file oriented. If regulated customer data is routed from aci into ComfyUI artifacts or prompts, retention and residency controls may diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the safest supported severity.
conditions: IF regulated customer data from aci is embedded into ComfyUI prompts, seeds, or files
IF the deployment has retention or residency requirements for CRM/email data
mitigations: Classify and exclude regulated fields from image-generation inputs
Set a short retention window for transferred artifacts
Document which data classes may cross from aci to ComfyUI
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing controls
